done.why: The world said I had used all 30 turns just as I was heading to put the painting in the trophy case.

about: A cut-down, rearranged Zork. The house, the trap door, a cellar, a troll to fight, and an art gallery with a painting to steal. Parts of the map are unfinished and marked with notes. The lantern and sword start in the living room.

ending.what: I was carrying the painting back to the trophy case when the turn cap hit.

moments.note: The trap door crashed shut behind me and I heard someone barring it.
The troll fight had real back-and-forth: a disarm, a recovery, then a beheading. The sword's glow warned me first.
The east and west exits from the troll room were dead ends ("Back soon", "does not go anywhere yet"). The world felt small.
"You can't get up there with what you're carrying" did not say which item was the problem.

wished: Put the painting in the trophy case and see whether that ended the game.
Know which carried item blocked the chimney.
More map beyond the troll room.

lines.line: The troll is disarmed by a subtle feint past his guard.
The passage to the east has not been finished. A note is pinned to the rock: "Back soon. -- The Management."
lines.why: A funny way to handle an unfinished area.

fun.why: Brisk and mostly smooth, with a good troll fight. Some exits were dead ends.

engagement.why: I wanted to see whether the painting ended the game, but the turn cap stopped me.

difficulty.why: The troll fell in a few swings and nothing else blocked me.

interestingness.why: Familiar Zork with rearranged items, plus the unfinished-area notes.

prose.why: Concise classic prose with a few witty touches.
